content:
C’est désormais officiel ! Fnatic a annoncé ce mercredi 25 novembre le recrutement de Martin « marteen » Pátek pour la saison 2027 du VCT EMEA. À 22 ans, le joueur tchèque sort d’une saison durant laquelle il s’est imposé comme l’un des duellistes les plus redoutables de la scène européenne. Grand artisan de la qualification historique de Gentle Mates pour les Masters de Santiago, marteen avait notamment marqué les esprits en pulvérisant deux records en l’espace d’une semaine lors du Kickoff.

Après avoir établi un nouveau record européen avec 106 éliminations sur une même série, le Tchèque avait fait encore plus fort face à Fnatic. Au terme d’une confrontation en cinq cartes, marteen avait enregistré 126 éliminations, effaçant ainsi le précédent record mondial de 124 éliminations sur une série du VCT. Une performance exceptionnelle qui avait largement contribué à envoyer Gentle Mates vers le premier tournoi international de son histoire sur VALORANT.

Le recrutement de marteen s’inscrit dans le cadre d’une profonde reconstruction chez Fnatic. Après une saison 2026 décevante, la structure britannique a décidé de tourner la page d’un cycle particulièrement fructueux, marqué notamment par deux sacres internationaux en 2023. Les départs de Boaster et d’Alfajer, tous deux pressentis chez Gentle Mates, ainsi que celui de crashies, symbolisent la fin de cette époque dorée.

Aux côtés de kaajak et de Chronicle, marteen devrait incarner le renouveau de Fnatic, qui mise sur la puissance de feu et la polyvalence de ses joueurs pour retrouver les sommets de la scène européenne. Le défi sera néanmoins de taille pour la formation britannique, qui devra rapidement trouver de nouveaux automatismes après avoir perdu plusieurs de ses cadres historiques. title: Can you get rid of your Ultimate Edition bonus cars in GTA 6?
content:
The Ultimate Edition of Grand Theft Auto 6 proved to be the most popular edition of the record-breaking game, even though it costs $100 compared to the base $80. Many players simply couldn’t pass up on all of the content being offered with the Ultimate Edition in GTA 6, which is a long list.

However, while some of the Ultimate Edition content is nice, players are finding that other parts of it can be a nuisance. Specifically, the cars that come with the edition can easily be surpassed by other vehicles in GTA 6. Unfortunately, players are discovering that Ultimate Edition cars can’t be sold or unregistered, so what do you do with them once they’ve been claimed?

If you’re here, then you likely went to Moses or a Pay ‘n’ Spray shop in GTA 6 to register a new car, but saw you’re out of owned vehicle slots. In an attempt to free up space, you went to sell or unregister an Ultimate Edition car you redeemed, but saw a message saying you’re unable to do so.

Specifically, if you view a “Bonus Vehicle” like Jason’s ’55 Stanier or the ’67 Vapid Dominator Buggy, you’ll see a locked icon next to the vehicle and the message: “You can’t sell bonus vehicles.”

So, what do you do about all those bonus vehicles clogging up space in your garage? At the moment, it seems there is no way to actually get rid of them in GTA 6 . As soon as you claim a bonus vehicle from the Ultimate Edition or your pre-order, it becomes a permanently stored vehicle for the rest of your playthrough.

We even tried purposely losing or destroying some of these vehicles, but to no avail; they still wound up back in our stored vehicles tab at a Pay ‘n’ Spray. Right now, this seems to be an oversight by Rockstar Games, as there are too few precious stored vehicle slots in GTA 6 for them to be taken up by vehicles that have no use.

title: Aion 2 Players Slam NC Over “Pay-To-Win” Update
content:
NC has been walking the fine line between free-to-play and pay-to-win with Aion 2 ever since the game’s global launch on October 5, but with today’s update, the game might just have crossed it.

At its core, Aion 2 is a free-to-play (F2P) game since the MMORPG is literally free on Steam. However, players have repeatedly raised concerns about the F2P experience being borderline “unplayable” due to the quality-of-life bonuses you can get upon purchasing a subscription.

Up until today, getting an Aion 2 subscription mostly sped up your progress, and no major progression was locked behind a paywall. The November 24 update changes that by adding a crucial progression feature to the “Wind Breeze Merchants” shop, a vendor available exclusively to subscribers.

For the unaware, today’s Aion 2 update unlocked the 5th Stigma slot for players. Players can use the extra Stigma slot for their characters by obtaining Stigma Shards in-game. To help players level up their newly added Stigma slot, this update also adds a total of 50 Stigma Shards that are obtainable through various means.

This is where the pay-to-win criticism comes in. Of those 50 Stigma Shards, 20 are locked behind the sub-only shop, meaning F2P players have no way to obtain them. For reference, 20 shards are enough to take a Stigma skill from level 0 all the way up to level 11 , with the max level of each skill being 20.

Shortly after the patch notes were revealed to the public, posts began surfacing on social media regarding NC’s decision to lock the Stigma Shards behind the sub-only shop.

title: CS2 Returns to the Esports World Cup in 2027 and 2028, With $700,000 for the Riyadh Champions
content:
Counter-Strike 2 is staying at the Esports World Cup for at least two more years. The Esports Foundation confirmed on 25 November that CS2 will return for EWC 2027 and EWC 2028 , which makes Valve’s shooter a fixture at the event for five straight years. More importantly for the teams, the 2027 edition comes with a firm date, a $2 million prize pool and a qualification system that rewards consistency across the whole first half of the season.

The tournament heads back to Esports Boulevard in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, after the 2026 finals were staged at the Accor Arena in Paris. It runs from 20 July to 1 August 2027 with 32 teams, while the 2028 edition is pencilled in for 14 to 30 July 2028. The organisers have not yet given a venue, format or prize pool for that second year, so for now 2027 is where the detail lies.

Every stage of the 2027 event is played in person, qualifier included. Stage 1 splits the 32 teams into four groups of eight, each run as a double-elimination bracket, and the top four from every group move on. The 16 survivors then meet in a Stage 2 playoff played as best-of-threes, with only the grand final stretched to a best-of-five. In practice, that means a team can afford one bad series in the groups but not two, which tends to favour deep, experienced rosters over hot streaks.

The money is weighted heavily towards the top. The champions take home $700,000, or roughly a third of the pool, while second place is worth $300,000, third $150,000 and fourth $90,000. Even so, nobody leaves empty-handed, since every team in the main event collects at least $10,000. The full payout table and schedule are on the official EWC 2027 Counter-Strike 2 page .

Most of the field is built from the Valve Regional Standings . Twenty places go to the best-ranked teams in the global standings, and North America, South America and Asia each get two more invites of their own, which guarantees those regions a presence however the global table looks. Two wildcard invites complete the direct list. Crucially, invitations follow the first monthly VRS publication of May 2027, and seeding uses the first ranking published in July. As a result, the first five months of next year effectively become the qualifier for most of the teams that will travel to Riyadh.

The last four places come from the Riyadh Open Qualifier on 16 to 18 July 2027, and this is where the format changes most. At EWC 2026, the final four spots went through a 64-team Last Chance Qualifier. Next year’s open qualifier allows up to 128 teams on a first-come, first-served basis, with a $100 entry fee and $100,000 shared among the teams that finish fifth to 16th. The entry fee is trivial, although the in-person, non-BYOC format means flights and hotels in Riyadh will be the real cost for any team chasing one of those four slots. Registration details have not been announced yet.

title: Solary : Sakor pousse un coup de gueule contre « le copinage » en LEC
content:
Malgré les excellentes performances de Solary et de Galions sur la scène européenne cette année, seuls cinq joueurs issus de ces deux formations devraient évoluer en LEC en 2027 : HARPOON, Thayger, Kryze, Zicssi et Piero. Un constat particulièrement frustrant pour Sakor Ros, qui estime que les dix joueurs méritaient leur chance dans l’élite européenne. Interrogé notamment sur l’absence de Zoelys, le cofondateur de Solary n’a pas mâché ses mots, dans des propos relayés par aAa . « Je pense que les dix ont leur place pour remplacer des joueurs en LEC, parce que la ligue est trop un cercle fermé de joueurs qui sont là depuis longtemps, donc on les fait tourner. »

Sakor regrette notamment que certaines organisations continuent de miser sur des joueurs expérimentés en raison de leurs succès passés, prenant l’exemple de Matyáš « Carzzy » Orság, attendu chez Movistar KOI après son départ de Vitality. Le dirigeant tourangeau dénonce plus globalement le manque d’ambition et de scouting de certaines structures européennes. « C’est ça aussi le problème du LEC : c’est du copinage. Tu as plein d’équipes qui sont là sans ambition, donc elles ne vont pas essayer d’aller scouter de nouveaux profils. Elles vont juste prendre des noms pour des noms sans les avoir vus jouer. »

Mais c’est surtout le retour pressenti de Mihael « Mikyx » Mehle chez G2 Esports qui fait bondir Sakor. Malgré l’immense palmarès du support slovène et ses précédents succès aux côtés de Hans sama, le cofondateur de Solary estime que les Samouraïs auraient dû se tourner vers un profil plus jeune. « Mikyx, je suis désolé, Mikyx qui revient chez G2, c’est de la merde. Voilà, c’est ridicule. Pour moi, il ne devrait plus être en LEC » , a-t-il lâché, regrettant également le recrutement de Skeanz par SK Gaming lors de la précédente intersaison.

Pour Sakor, G2 aurait notamment pu donner sa chance à Piero ou à Zoelys, dont il apprécie particulièrement les qualités en phase de lane. « Le prime de Mikyx est passé. Moi, je n’aurais pas trouvé ça déconnant de prendre un autre support, genre justement un G2 qui va chercher un Piero, ou même un Zoelys. Je pense que ça aurait pu fonctionner. » Au-delà du cas de Mikyx, cette sortie médiatique relance le débat sur les passerelles entre les ligues régionales et le LEC, alors que de nombreux talents continuent de se heurter aux portes de l’élite européenne malgré leurs performances en ERL.

title: GTA 6’s ‘Woke’ Backlash Over Jason and Lucia Relationship
content:
The row over whether Grand Theft Auto VI has gone “woke” has spilled out of streams and X threads and into mainstream news. AFP’s wire story on 25 November asked whether the series had gone soft . CBC News then reported that some streamers find the game too woke , while WIRED ran a piece on 19 November about men online who are angry that the game rewards being a good partner. The complaints centre on Jason and Lucia’s relationship, a new system that scores how players behave, and the absence of sex workers for the first time since GTA III.

The backlash sits awkwardly next to the numbers. GTA VI made about .8 billion on its first day, as our report on its record launch revenue covers, and it holds a 99 Metascore, as our reviews roundup found. That gap between the loudest critics and the wider audience is exactly what has drawn reporters in.

Most of the anger is about what the game asks players to do between heists. Players are encouraged to look after the relationship by fixing up Jason and Lucia’s house, buying flowers and jewellery, and running errands such as picking up groceries for Lucia. Some anonymous X users have called the result “feminist slop”, while others have reached for a slur borrowed from manosphere forums, according to AFP. Several streamers have also complained that too much of the early story is made up of errand-style missions.

The second target is the behaviour system, which AFP describes as an honour system. Citing video game press reports, the agency said players earn focus and behaviour points for acts such as kindness to strangers, not littering and staying fit. The happiest ending reportedly needs a strong relationship and a professional criminal profile rather than a violent or psycho one, which critics argue is a strange fit for a series built on chaos.

Fans who miss the older games also point to the removal of sex workers, a feature the series had carried since GTA III in 2001, as our report on why Rockstar removed it explains. For many of the angriest players, that single change has become a symbol of everything they think the series has lost. Others simply argue that the game has become less of a sandbox and more of a guided story.

Rockstar has framed the changes as a matter of story. The studio told AFP that GTA VI is about a couple in trouble and on the run together, and that its design choices were made to serve that story. Rockstar North’s Rob Nelson made a similar point before launch, saying the game offers optional ways to show empathy for players who want them, as our report on his comments and the criminal profile explains.

title: Woman Asks Instagram How to Cash Out Her Boyfriend’s CS2 Skins, Gets Roasted Instead

The inventory in the photo is the kind that many CS2 players spend years building, with several knives and pairs of gloves sitting in the top rows.

title: BGMI Air vs BGMI on the Same Phone: 60 FPS vs 40, Zero Ads and No 2.4GB Download
content:
BGMI Air’s open beta went live on the Google Play Store at 10am IST on 25 November, and by lunchtime X was full of posts claiming that the lighter version of Battlegrounds Mobile India lags badly and pushes ads at players. We installed it the same morning and played a full Classic match on Erangel to see how much of that holds up. Across roughly 14 minutes of recorded play, the ping readout never moved from 20ms, not a single ad appeared, and the game let us drop into a 100-player match without forcing any extra download first.

One phone and one match cannot settle the question for every device, of course, and Air makes some visible trade-offs to stay this small. To put the numbers in context, we then installed the main BGMI on the same phone, signed in with the same account and played it too. Below is everything we found, set against what KRAFTON has confirmed so far and what other early testers are reporting.

The lag complaints were the main reason we wanted to test Air ourselves, so we kept an eye on the network readout in the bottom corner of the screen throughout. From the plane and the drop towards Georgopol, through a buggy ride across the map, to a firefight in which we knocked down an enemy, it read 20ms every time we checked, on Wi-Fi and on the India server. Going back through the recording afterwards, we found no rubber-banding and no frozen frames either.

Smoothness held up just as well. Our screen recording averaged about 58 frames per second over the session, which suggests the game was running close to 60 FPS for most of the match. A screen recorder is not a proper frame counter, so treat that figure as a strong hint rather than a benchmark. It is also worth saying that our test phone runs the main game too, which means this result tells you little about how Air behaves on a 2GB budget handset, the kind of device it was actually built for. That test is next on our list.

The ad worry appears to trace back to an Instagram story from the creator LetsGrow about irrelevant ads playing while the lobby sat idle, according to the esports account Esports360 (@Esports360igc). Esports360 then tried it in both BGMI and BGMI Air, leaving each game idle in the lobby for five to six minutes, and reported that no ad appeared in either.

Our session lines up with that. We spent time in the lobby, opened the Download Center, waited through matchmaking on the spawn island and played the match out, and at no point did a video or banner ad show up. Live service games can switch features on from the server whenever the developer chooses, so that could change before or after launch, but on the evidence so far the ad claims look unproven.

title: Apex Legends Cheaters Stayed in Matches for Up to 4 Hours
content:
Respawn says its new EA Javelin anti-cheat bans 51% more Apex Legends cheaters than Easy Anti-Cheat did. The studio also admitted that detected cheaters could keep playing for up to four hours before a ban landed.

Respawn says its new EA Javelin anti-cheat bans 51% more Apex Legends cheaters than Easy Anti-Cheat did. The studio also admitted that detected cheaters could keep playing for up to four hours before a ban landed.

The admission came in a two-month review of Javelin, which took over PC anti-cheat duties at the end of September. Respawn says a new enforcement system, live this week, has cut the wait between detection and ban to as little as one match.

Javelin is built by a team inside Electronic Arts, which gives Respawn a direct line to the engineers who maintain it. The studio says that speeds up investigations and its response to new cheats, and it backs legal action against cheat makers and sellers, including cease-and-desist notices.

The system runs at the kernel level, so it sees deeper into a player's machine. Respawn says that helps against malicious or vulnerable drivers, virtualization, unauthorized controller hardware and software, and DMA (direct memory access) devices.

The rollout was cautious. Several lower-level protections were switched off at launch and enabled gradually as the team grew confident in their stability. An issue hit the EA App shortly after launch and was fixed the next day.

title: MrBeast Gaming Overtakes IShowSpeed as GTA 6 Launch Week Views Hit 1.77 Billion
content:
MrBeast Gaming has overtaken IShowSpeed as the YouTube channel gaining the most views from Grand Theft Auto VI’s launch week. MrBeast’s gaming channel had added 269.9 million public views by 25 November, against 232.9 million for IShowSpeed, according to PUNKSQUAD’s GTA VI launch tracker . Speed led comfortably for the first few days, but a huge two-day surge early this week carried MrBeast Gaming past him.

The tracker follows 127 channels streaming the game, and together they have picked up 1.77 billion public views since 18 November, the day before launch. Those channels have a combined 1.15 billion subscribers, which gives a sense of how far GTA VI has spread across YouTube in a single week. The surge on YouTube follows a record on Twitch as well, as our report on the game’s 7.1 million peak viewers at launch covers.

IShowSpeed made the much faster start of the two. His channel added 37.4 million views in the first daily snapshot after launch and another 61.3 million in the next, so he was close to 100 million before MrBeast Gaming had reached 30 million. By the snapshot on 22 November, Speed still led by 138.7 million to 94.7 million.

The gap then closed in just two days. MrBeast Gaming added 74.7 million views in the 23 November snapshot and 71.4 million in the next, the two biggest single-day gains of any channel on the list all week. That run took it from 94.7 million to 240.8 million and past Speed, who added 40.8 million and 35.4 million over the same two days.

The lead has kept growing since then, with 29.1 million more views for MrBeast Gaming in the 25 November snapshot against 18.0 million for Speed. MrBeast Gaming is the gaming offshoot of MrBeast, whose main channel is the most subscribed on YouTube. It now has 62.8 million subscribers of its own, almost level with Speed’s 63.3 million. The main channel has been setting records of its own this year too, as our report on his record-breaking grocery store challenge shows.

Techno Gamerz sits third with 112.2 million, well clear of a tight group below him. IGN’s channel is fourth on 76.8 million, just ahead of Kai Cenat Live on 72.5 million, while DarkViperAU , best known for his GTA V speedruns and commentary, is sixth with 69.4 million. title: That Leaked GTA 6 Online Press Release Is Fake, and It Admits It in the Last Line
content:
A document dressed up as an official Rockstar Games press release for GTA VI’s online mode is spreading on X, claiming that it launches in March 2027 on every platform, PC included. The document is not a real Rockstar release. Rockstar has published no such announcement on its Newswire , and the document’s own closing line admits that “Rockstar Games has not announced a date for GTA VI Online”.

The image was posted on 24 November by an X account created in July 2026, which said it found the document “2 months before Rockstar planned to announce it”. The same post said “i was using Fable”, the name of an AI model, and the footer of the image reads “by Fable 5.2”. Earlier posts from the account claimed to have replaced Rockstar’s entire QA team with the same AI model, which tells you most of what you need to know about where this came from.

official GTA 6 Online launch date just leaked. March 2027, every platform, PC from day one. Rockstar is putting $780 million into it before it even goes live i found this 2 months before Rockstar planned to announce it. they tried to get it taken down twice. i was using Fable… pic.twitter.com/oCbBgrVuEr

Real press releases announce things, but this one argues with itself. Its headline says Rockstar “Announces Grand Theft Auto Online for Grand Theft Auto VI Now Available”, its dateline reads March 2027, and its first paragraph says the mode “is now live”. Yet it appeared online in November 2026, and it ends by saying no date has been announced at all.

The structure of the document gives it away even faster. It includes sections titled “Why This Window” and “What Rockstar Still Has to Solve Before Launch”, which list server stability, a missing 60fps mode and single-player bugs as open problems. No publisher lists its own unresolved worries in a launch announcement, and none cites news reports and analyst estimates as its sources, which this document does throughout.

The numbers in it do not hold up to a basic check either. title: BGMI Air FPS: How Much FPS Does BGMI Air Support? All 7 Frame Rate Options Explained
content:
BGMI Air is KRAFTON India’s lighter version of Battlegrounds Mobile India, built to run on budget phones with less storage and memory. For many players, the first question is how smooth it can run, because frame rate decides how responsive aiming, recoil control and movement feel in a fight.

The answer depends on your phone. BGMI Air keeps the same frame rate ladder as the main game, but which options you can select is decided by your device’s chipset, RAM and display refresh rate.

BGMI Air lists frame rate options from 20 FPS up to 120 FPS. Its Frame Rate Settings menu shows seven levels: Power Saving, Medium, High, Ultra, Extreme, Extreme+ and Ultra Extreme. On most budget and mid range phones, the highest option available is Extreme, which runs the game at 60 FPS.

The two highest settings, Extreme+ (90 FPS) and Ultra Extreme (120 FPS), appear greyed out on phones that do not support them. These options only unlock on devices with a high refresh rate display and a chipset strong enough to hold that frame rate, the same rule KRAFTON India applies in the main game.

Each frame rate level in BGMI Air matches a target number of frames per second. Higher settings feel smoother but use more battery and produce more heat.

The lowest setting caps the game at 20 FPS. It is meant for very old phones or for saving battery, but the low frame rate makes fast fights and aiming noticeably harder.

title: Fake GTA 6 PC Downloads Are Spreading Malware After the Biggest Port Project Vanished
content:
The biggest effort to turn the leaked Xbox build of Grand Theft Auto VI into a playable PC game has gone offline, and the scammers are filling the gap. Project Leonida’s GitHub page and Discord server both disappeared late on 23 November, US time, only hours after Cyberleek released the build’s missing executable. Security researchers have warned for months that fake GTA VI downloads are a favourite way to spread malware. With the best-known port project gone, those fakes are now the bigger risk for anyone hunting for a PC version.

None of the PC port efforts was ever an official release, and Rockstar Games still has not announced a PC version of the game. Our report on the first PC port claims covered how far the modders said they had got. Since then, the story has shifted from what the leaked build can do to what downloading it can do to your computer.

Leonida was an open-source effort to rebuild the leaked Xbox code so that it would run natively on Windows. Before it went offline, its GitHub repository had more than 34,000 stars, over 400 contributors and more than 3,000 copies made by other users. Late on 23 November, Eastern time, the repository moved to a new account and then stopped loading altogether, and the project’s main Discord server, with around 179,000 members, vanished soon afterwards.

The project’s creator posted a short message on X shortly after the shutdown: “I quit guys. I’m sorry.” He has said that Rockstar was behind the removal of the Discord server, but Rockstar, Take-Two Interactive and Discord have not commented publicly. GitHub publishes the copyright notices it receives in a public DMCA archive , and no notice against Leonida had appeared there at the time of reporting, so it is still not confirmed who removed the repository.

Take-Two does have a long record of using copyright takedowns against unofficial versions of its games, including hundreds of unofficial GTA V mobile ports on GitHub in the run-up to GTA VI’s launch. It has also used US court subpoenas against Microsoft and Discord this year in its hunt for Cyberleek, as our explainer on the leaker sets out. Chief executive Strauss Zelnick said before launch that the company expected the game to be pirated, as our report on his comments covered.

The fakes are not new, but the leak has given them a fresh hook. Security firm Huntress found in September that one fake GTA 6 installer showed a “license not found” message to make victims think the game had simply failed to install. In the background, it dropped remote access tools, a stealer for passwords and Discord tokens, and a ransomware strain that Huntress said behaved like a wiper, destroying files rather than holding them for ransom.

title: GTA 6 Runs Smoother on Xbox Series X Than PS5, PS5 Pro the Best
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI runs more smoothly on Xbox Series X than on a standard PS5, according to Digital Foundry’s comparison of every console version. The two consoles share the same core settings and a very similar image, but the PS5 drops more frames, particularly when players are driving at speed through Vice City. The best version of all is on PS5 Pro, while the Xbox Series S is the one Digital Foundry found hardest to recommend.

The result has drawn attention because Sony has been the face of the game’s marketing, and PlayStation has called GTA VI the biggest launch in its history. More than 39 million players have played it on PS5 since launch, as our PlayStation launch record report covers, so the base console’s performance matters to a huge audience. Every version targets 30 frames per second, as our report on the Xbox 60fps glitch explains, so small dips below that target are easy to feel.

Digital Foundry found that the Xbox Series X and the base PS5 both output a softer image at around 1440p, with matching key settings. In some areas the Series X has small resolution advantages and slightly higher-quality visuals, though it also shows occasional blurriness and some missing shadows. Overall, Digital Foundry said the game “acquits itself quite well” on Microsoft’s most powerful console.

The bigger difference is in frame rate rather than image quality. “In typical play, both of them hit 30 FPS or don’t fall far below,” Digital Foundry said, but the PS5 dips more often than its rival. During fast driving, Digital Foundry said, “PS5 seems substantially worse off in this respect”, although chases and explosions can still pull the Series X below its target too.

That gap will surprise many players, since PlayStation has handled much of the game’s marketing. It is also a reminder that the two machines are close in power, and that small differences in how a game handles heavy scenes can decide which version feels steadier. On paper, the Series X has the stronger graphics chip, rated at about 12 teraflops against roughly 10.3 for the PS5, while the PS5 has the faster storage drive. Busy driving sequences lean heavily on the graphics chip, which may help explain where the Xbox pulls ahead. Rockstar has already released updates since launch, as our guide to update 01.002.002 covers, and future patches could narrow the difference.

The PS5 Pro version stands clear of the rest. Digital Foundry described its image as “4K-like”, with solid frame rates and ray-traced shadows that give a noticeable upgrade over the other consoles. It called the Pro version “the best option available”, which will reassure players who bought Sony’s most expensive console with this game in mind. The Pro launched in November 2024 as Sony’s upgraded PS5, with a stronger graphics chip and better ray tracing, and GTA VI is exactly the kind of game it was built to show off.

title: Krafton Earns ₹6,840 Crore in Q3 2026 as Profit Falls 35.5%, BGMI Air Crosses 14 Million Pre-Registrations
content:
Krafton earned ₩971.4 billion (about ₹6,840 crore or $728 million) in revenue in the third quarter of 2026, its latest results, up 11.6% from a year earlier. Operating profit fell 35.5% to ₩225 billion (about ₹1,584 crore or $169 million), and currency losses left the BGMI publisher with a net loss of ₩68.4 billion (about ₹482 crore or $51 million).

India featured prominently in the quarter, even though Krafton does not report revenue by country. The company pointed to BGMI Air’s pre-registration numbers on its earnings call, and Krafton India announced a fresh investment pledge that takes the group’s planned spending in the country past $500 million (about ₹4,700 crore).

Krafton reported the results on 10 November for the July to September quarter. Revenue rose from ₩870.6 billion (about ₹6,130 crore or $652 million) a year earlier, while operating profit fell mainly because of lower PC revenue and costs linked to gamescom.

Mobile remained Krafton’s largest business at ₩504.3 billion (about ₹3,551 crore or $378 million), up 3.2% year on year and 12% on the previous quarter. BGMI’s revenue sits inside this mobile figure, along with PUBG Mobile. PC revenue fell 32.5% to ₩238.9 billion (about ₹1,682 crore or $179 million), and console revenue was ₩8.6 billion (about ₹61 crore or $6.4 million).

Other revenue reached ₩219.6 billion (about ₹1,546 crore or $165 million), almost all of it from ₩198.4 billion (about ₹1,397 crore or $149 million) in advertising and content income from Japan’s ADK Group. A full breakdown of the quarter is in our report on Krafton’s Q3 2026 results .

Over the first nine months of 2026, Krafton posted record revenue of ₩3.633 trillion (about ₹25,581 crore or $2.72 billion), up 51%. Nine month operating profit reached ₩1.1975 trillion (about ₹8,432 crore or $897 million), up 14% and already above its full year profit for 2025.

title: LCS : après G2 NORD, Toasty va découvrir l’élite avec OpTic Gaming

OpTic Gaming poursuit la construction de son effectif en vue de son grand retour sur League of Legends. Le joueur de 20 ans aurait notamment été préféré à APA, également considéré par la direction. Déjà courtisé par Dignitas lors de la précédente intersaison, Toasty va finalement avoir l’opportunité de faire ses débuts dans l’élite nord-américaine.

Passé par plusieurs formations du circuit académique nord-américain depuis ses débuts en 2021, Toasty avait fait le choix de rejoindre l’Europe en 2026 pour intégrer le nouveau projet de G2 NORD. Une expérience concluante pour le jeune Américain, qui a remporté le Spring Split de Prime League et atteint les finales des segments hivernal et estival. Il a également participé aux trois éditions des EMEA Masters cette année, atteignant à chaque fois le Top 8. Des performances qui lui ouvrent désormais les portes des LCS.

Sept ans après sa dernière apparition dans le championnat nord-américain, OpTic Gaming s’apprête à retrouver les LCS grâce à un nouveau partenariat avec Riot Games. La célèbre organisation, principalement connue pour ses succès sur Call of Duty, prendra la place de Dignitas en 2027, sans toutefois devenir propriétaire de son slot. Lors de son premier passage dans la compétition, entre 2018 et 2019, OpTic n’avait jamais réussi à faire mieux qu’une cinquième place, malgré la présence de joueurs renommés comme Dhokla et Crown, champion du monde en 2017.

Pour son retour, la structure américaine semble vouloir miser sur la jeunesse. Après avoir trouvé un accord avec le jungler canadien KryRa, OpTic Gaming devrait donc compléter son duo jungle-mid avec Toasty. Deux jeunes joueurs désireux de faire leurs preuves au plus haut niveau, autour desquels l’organisation pourrait construire un projet sur le long terme. Pour Toasty, qui fêtera ses 21 ans en janvier, cette arrivée représente surtout une belle opportunité de confirmer les progrès réalisés durant son passage en Europe.

title: GTA 6 Marbelle Hotel Safe Code and Location

Unlike most safes in Leonida, it needs a six digit code, and the game hides that code behind a short horror sequence.

This guide covers the safe code, where to find the safe, how to reveal the code yourself and everything the safe contains.

The Marbelle Hotel safe code in GTA 6 is 955214 . Players can enter it straight away if they go directly to the safe, without completing the event on the upper floors first.

Most safes in the game use four digit codes, so the six digit combination is one of the clues that the Marbelle Hotel is a special location. Opening the safe also clears the heavy fog that settles over Vice City during the event.

The Marbelle Hotel sits on NW 8th Street in southern Crosstown, Vice City, next to the highway and east of the Pawn and Gun shop. The front of the building is closed, so players need to walk down the alley on the left side and use the unlocked back door.

The safe is in the ground floor office. Walk past the staircase to find a grey safe in the corner, next to a red desk.

title: s1mple’s Major Return Turns Into a Nightmare as GOSH Fall to 0-2 in Singapore
content:
s1mple’s return to the Major stage has started about as badly as it possibly could. His team, playing as GOSH at the PGL Major Singapore 2026, lost both of its opening matches in Stage 1 on 24 November and won just four rounds across two maps. The defeats leave GOSH at 0-2 in the Swiss bracket, one more loss away from going home before the Major has properly begun.

Team Liquid beat them 13-1 on Nuke in the opening round, and FaZe followed with a 13-3 win on Mirage later the same day. GOSH now face Chinggis Warriors in a best-of-three elimination match on 25 November, with no margin left for error. Our Stage 1 preview explains how the first stage works, and day one went very differently from what s1mple and his teammates had planned.

The Liquid match was effectively over almost as soon as it started. Liquid won 13 of the 14 rounds on Nuke, and s1mple finished with four kills and 12 deaths for a 0.53 rating, according to HLTV’s match statistics. Statistician NarT noted that it was the second-worst individual map of s1mple’s Major career, and he was not even the lowest-rated player on his team, as Emil “Magisk” Reif went 3-14.

The FaZe match gave a little more from s1mple, but no more hope for his team. He finished 11-14 with a 0.91 rating, level with Tyson “asap” Paterson as the best on GOSH, while Azbayar “Senzu” Munkhbold managed just three kills. FaZe’s Russel “Twistzz” Van Dulken led the server with 21 kills and a 1.77 rating, as FaZe bounced back from their own 13-9 loss to Wildcard in the first round.

Across the two maps, GOSH won four rounds and lost 26, which is a brutal return for a lineup that arrived with real expectations. The team brought s1mple, Magisk, Senzu, Ayush “mzinho” Batbold and asap to Singapore, a mix of veteran stars and young talent. Our players to watch list and Pick’Em guide set out the stakes for the stage before a single map was played. The results are also a blow for fans who backed GOSH in Valve’s Pick’Em challenge, where players predict which teams finish 3-0, which finish 0-3 and which advance from each stage.

GOSH is not the team’s usual name, and the change has nothing to do with its results. PGL confirmed on 9 November that four teams would play under different names in Singapore, because the companies behind them are not licensed under the country’s gambling rules, as our report on the name changes explains. The team took the name of GOSH, a live-streaming platform it recently partnered with, and PGL’s announcement on X listed the other three renamed teams.

title: GTA 6 Is Already Booting on PC After Cyberleek Leaks the Missing File
content:
Five days after Grand Theft Auto VI launched on consoles, modders say they already have a leaked Xbox version of the game booting on Windows PCs. The claims follow the release of the build’s main executable file by Cyberleek, the anonymous leaker behind months of stolen GTA VI footage, on 23 November. Rockstar Games has not announced a PC version, and neither it nor Take-Two Interactive has commented publicly on the leak.

None of the progress has been independently verified, and almost all of it comes from video clips and posts on X. Even so, the clips have spread quickly across social media, along with bold claims that the game is “fully booting up” on ordinary gaming PCs. Cyberleek first put the rest of the build online on launch day, as our report on the Xbox build leak explained.

Cyberleek had promised to release the executable on 23 November, or sooner if the market value of its own crypto token reached $15 million. The file began circulating shortly before 3pm UTC that day, a few hours ahead of the leaker’s own schedule, according to accounts tracking the release. The rest of the build, which Cyberleek says is around 209GB, had been online since 19 November, but without the executable the game could not run.

Cyberleek published checksums alongside the file so that people could compare copies, but matching checksums do not prove that a build is genuine or complete. The executable also cannot simply be launched on a Windows PC like a normal game. A modder who posts as Chasm on X wrote that people would “need to get to work recomping it for PC”, which means rebuilding the Xbox code so that it runs on Windows.

Progress has been faster than many people expected. Within hours of the release, clips showed the leaked build reaching its opening settings screens on PC, and by the evening of 23 November Chasm was claiming the game was “fully booting up”. On 24 November the same account said shaders were “working somewhat” and that the visuals could be right by the end of the day, with performance still to be fixed after that.

Some posts go further and claim the game has reached its prologue on PC, but at around 3 frames per second with broken textures and barely working lighting, and TalkEsport could not verify them. Part of the reason the work is moving quickly is that Xbox games are built with Microsoft’s Game Development Kit , which shares much of its foundation with Windows. That does not make a finished port simple, though, as missing system files and anti-tamper protection remain serious hurdles.

title: Trump Says He Backed Jensen Huang’s Return as Lawmakers From Both Parties Demand Answers
content:
President Donald Trump has said he recommended that Nvidia’s board bring back Jensen Huang, a day after the chipmaker reinstated him as chief executive. Speaking to reporters on 23 November, Trump said he was “very, very happy” that the board “had the courage to do the right thing”. Lawmakers from both parties have since made clear that Huang’s return does not end their questions about Nvidia, China and the role of US officials in the decision.

Huang is now due to face three days of questioning in Washington at the start of December. Two days of transcribed interviews with House committees are set for 1 and 2 December, followed by a public hearing in the Senate on 3 December, according to the Associated Press. Our report on Huang’s reinstatement covers the board’s decision in full.

Trump’s comments, shared by the White House’s rapid response account, suggest he was directly involved in the outcome. “If I thought that he did something wrong, I wouldn’t be recommending to his board to hire him,” he said in one clip . The Associated Press also reported him saying that the board had done “what we wanted them to do”.

Trump also dismissed the reports that Huang had been targeted by a Chinese intelligence effort through a businesswoman US authorities suspect of spying. “With Jensen, I don’t believe that’s true,” he said, in remarks posted by the same account. Asked whether critics were right that Huang was now too big to fail, Trump said “No” and called him “a brilliant guy”, according to another clip .

Nvidia’s own filing with the SEC said the board had received input from “senior levels of the United States government”. It also said the board was confident that Huang’s return “poses no national security risk”. That marked a sharp turn from mid-November, when Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for an outside chief executive, as our Bessent report explains. Bessent has also said he was frustrated by the Commerce Department’s delay in restricting Nvidia chip exports to Megaspeed, the AP reported.

Some of the sharpest pushback came from Trump’s own party. Three Republican committee chairs, John Moolenaar, Rick Crawford and Brian Mast, said in a joint statement that the board’s brief review did not “erase the national security threats and questions that must be addressed”. The statement, also published by the House Foreign Affairs Committee , said they still wanted answers on the smuggling of Nvidia products to China.

title: Team Liquid Licenses Its Brand to Friendly Fire, Turning 22 Gaming Cafes Into Team Liquid Cafes
content:
Team Liquid has licensed its brand to Croatian gaming cafe franchisor Friendly Fire in a 10 year deal, turning 22 existing venues across Europe into Team Liquid Cafes. The esports organisation will earn royalties and commissions from the branded locations and will become a shareholder in Friendly Fire. Financial terms were not disclosed.

The partners plan to open a flagship in Utrecht, the Dutch city where Team Liquid was founded in 2000, followed by flagships in Houston and Miami in 2027. Asia and the Middle East are also being lined up as future markets.

Team Liquid supplies its brand, content, players and creators, and consumer products to the cafes. Friendly Fire, led by founder and chief executive David Kosir, runs oversight and day to day operations across the network. Individual franchisees put up the money to build and run each venue.

Team Liquid will receive royalties and commissions on income from branded locations, along with an equity stake in Friendly Fire. Chief executive Steve Arhancet did not disclose the size of that stake or whether Team Liquid is investing any capital in the company. The full announcement is on Team Liquid’s website .

For franchisees, the cost of entry is significant. Friendly Fire’s terms put a single location at roughly $218,400 to $390,685, including a $49,500 franchise fee.

The venues are built around high end gaming PCs, sim racing rigs and consoles, along with lounge areas and local tournaments. Team Liquid co chief executive Victor Goossens said the partners plan to open hundreds more venues in the coming years.

title: BLG's Worlds 2026 Final Sets Bilibili Record at 32.42M Views
content:
The Worlds 2026 final between BLG and Gen.G is now the most-viewed League of Legends match in Bilibili history. Its replay has reached 32.42 million views, enough to pass the 2018 final between Fnatic and Invictus Gaming.

BLG won their first world title, and the match is now a record holder away from the game too. The replay of their 3-1 win over Gen.G has reached 32.42 million views on Bilibili, the Chinese video platform often compared to YouTube. No League of Legends match has been watched more often there.

The old leader was the Worlds 2018 final, where Invictus Gaming beat Fnatic. That replay stands at 32.39 million views, so BLG lead by only about 30,000. The 2021 final between EDward Gaming and DWG KIA is third with 32.11 million.

All three matches ended with an LPL team lifting the Summoner's Cup. In 2018 Invictus Gaming beat Fnatic 3-0, which gave China its first world title. The 2021 final went to EDward Gaming, 3-2 over DWG KIA. AD carry Park Do-hyeon, known as Viper, links two of the three finals. He won with EDward Gaming in 2021 and again with BLG in 2026. He is one of two players to win Worlds twice on teams that did not include Faker.

The replay passed 19.9 million views in its first 24 hours. That was already more than the roughly 15.9 million views the 2024 final between BLG and T1 collected on the platform. Viewers also sent more than 3.3 million scrolling comments, known as danmaku, while the match was live.

Numbers from outside mainland China tell a different story. The final peaked at 3,981,986 concurrent viewers on the platforms tracked internationally. That is 41% lower than the 2025 final, which reached 6,752,585, and the smallest Worlds final peak since the 2020 edition. The all-time record is still the 2024 final between T1 and BLG at 6,941,610. Our Worlds 2024 finals page covers that series.

title: LPL : BLG prêt à faire des folies pour retenir Viper, Ruler en plan B ?
content:
Bilibili Gaming s’apprête à vivre une intersaison mouvementée malgré une année 2026 exceptionnelle, couronnée par un titre de champion du monde face à Gen.G. Si Xun, Knight et ON sont encore sous contrat pour la saison prochaine, l’avenir de Bin et de Park « Viper » Do-hyeon reste incertain. Selon plusieurs rumeurs en provenance de Chine, relayées notamment par Caedrel et aAa , les dirigeants de BLG se seraient même rendus en Corée du Sud pour tenter de convaincre leur ADC de poursuivre l’aventure en LPL.

Pour retenir le double champion du monde, Bilibili Gaming serait prêt à lui offrir une augmentation salariale de 50 %, portant sa rémunération annuelle à environ 2,25 millions de dollars. Le club chinois lui aurait également proposé une pause rémunérée durant l’intégralité du premier segment de la saison 2027, ainsi que la mise à disposition d’un jet privé pour faciliter ses déplacements vers la Corée du Sud. Malgré ces conditions particulièrement avantageuses, Viper privilégierait un retour en LCK pour des raisons familiales. Kiwoom DRX figure notamment parmi ses destinations potentielles.

Consciente du risque de perdre son ADC, la direction de Bilibili Gaming étudierait déjà plusieurs alternatives. Parmi elles figure un autre grand nom de la scène internationale : Park « Ruler » Jae-hyuk. Le champion du monde 2017 pourrait ainsi retrouver Knight, avec lequel il avait réalisé une saison 2023 exceptionnelle sous les couleurs de JD Gaming. Cette piste intervient alors que Gen.G traverse également une intersaison agitée, marquée par les départs de Kiin et Canyon, tous deux pressentis chez Hanwha Life Esports.

Le recrutement de Ruler s’annonce toutefois particulièrement complexe. Contrairement à Viper, l’ancien joueur de JD Gaming dispose encore d’un contrat jusqu’à la fin de la saison 2027, ce qui obligerait BLG à négocier une indemnité de transfert avec Gen.G. Rien n’indique par ailleurs que le principal intéressé souhaite retourner en Chine. Pour l’heure, la priorité de Bilibili Gaming reste donc de convaincre Viper de prolonger son aventure. La décision du champion du monde pourrait bien provoquer un véritable jeu de chaises musicales entre la LPL et la LCK.

Son retour en France constitue donc une excellente nouvelle pour Solary, qui récupère un joueur expérimenté et habitué à jouer les premiers rôles en LFL.

Après plusieurs années de désillusion, Solary a enfin connu la consécration en 2026. Le défi sera désormais de confirmer les succès de 2026 et de s’installer durablement au sommet de la scène européenne de deuxième division. title: Lynn Vision recover from 7-11 to extend 9z’s slump to eight
content:
Asia’s last qualifiers won the final six rounds on their CT side.

Lynn Vision beat 9z 13-11 on Inferno in the opening round of Stage 1 at the PGL Major Singapore 2026 , winning the last six rounds after trailing 7-11. The defeat is the eighth in a row for 9z , the organisation’s longest losing run since April 2019, while the lowest seed in the stage open with a win.

For most of the second half, the story was 9z finally shaking off their run. history, standing in for the benched meyern, opened it with a double kill to win the pistol round, and 9z took the first four rounds on their T side. dgt then won a clutch on 22 HP after Starry let him off with a missed shot, and Lynn Vision called a timeout at 6-10.

The round that made it 11-7 looked like the end. Starry won the fights on a B retake, but he had no defuse kit, and the bomb went off before he could get it done. Lynn Vision had spent the half short of money, and 9z were two rounds from a first win since the start of their slide.

The answer came on the CT side. z4kr denied the plant on the next round, Westmelon took a double kill on the one after, and Lynn Vision suddenly had money while 9z were fighting with Galils and Tec-9s. At 10-11 they gambled with an aggressive push down middle and caught 9z mid-execute to level it. They ran the same idea again, C4LLM3SU3 sprinting down mid to clean up, and max, left alone on 24 HP, could not save the round that made it 12-11. z4kr took two kills on the final round, and luchov was left on 22 HP with nobody to trade him.

Starry led the server with 21 kills and 91.7% KAST, and C4LLM3SU3 had the best ADR at 89.6. luchov was 9z’s best player with 19 kills and 95.8% KAST. history ended 14-19 in his first match for the team at the Major.

title: Imperial win 12 straight rounds to sink HEROIC on Mirage
content:
Down 6-1 against the favourites, the Brazilians did not drop another round and took the first upset of the Singapore Major 13-6.

From 1-6 down, Imperial won every remaining round to beat HEROIC 13-6 on Mirage in the opening round of Stage 1 at the PGL Major Singapore 2026 . decenty led the server with 19 kills, saadzin died only five times, and a side ranked 37th by Valve left the side ranked 18th without a single round on their T side.

The veto did HEROIC no favours. They removed Inferno and Nuke, two maps they had won more than 70 per cent of the time over the last three months, and the process ran out on Mirage: their only losing map in our Stage 1 map guide , and one they had lost three times in a row coming into Singapore. Imperial had won 11 of their 16 Mirage games in the same guide.

For half an hour none of that seemed to matter. Chr1zN stalled saadzin long enough to deny the plant in the pistol round, and HEROIC were 5-0 up before Imperial had a round on the board. The fourth of those summed up the start for the Brazilians: decenty fought a lone battle on B, while saadzin waited in the top mid boxes for around 20 seconds and rotated too late to stop the defuse.

The game turned at 6-2. HEROIC had Imperial pinned in a post-plant, but MartinezSa’s flash landed just short in CT, the Terrorists were never blinded, and saadzin won the round with his AWP. Imperial broke HEROIC’s economy on the next one, noway took four kills against their pistols on the one after, and VINI closed out the final round of the half to make it 6-6.

The second half was all Imperial. They won the pistol round, read a B push perfectly with a stack, and then VINI rotated in alone to take four kills on a retake HEROIC looked set to win. decenty opened the next round with a double, and HEROIC never found a close round again. Chr1zN finished with 17 kills and 102.3 ADR; Brollan and nilo managed six kills each.

title: Can you return to Jason’s Key Lento house in GTA 6?
content:
For the first 25% of the main story in Grand Theft Auto 6, you play as Jason, who’s living out of a house right on the coast in Key Lento. The house belongs to Brian Heder, Jason’s boss, but he’s allowed to stay there as long as he keeps working. The house itself is a bit of a work in progress, as Jason needs to do some chores before Lucia comes home. However, after some sweat is shed, Jason’s house in Key Lento looks pretty decent in GTA 6.

Following the events of Chapter 1, though, the house is in a much different state. If you’ve completed Chapter 1, then you might be wondering if the Key Lento house can be returned to, especially considering you had some money stashed away there. Below, you can see exactly what happens if you go back to the safehouse during Chapter 2 and beyond in GTA 6.

Warning: There are spoilers for the main story in GTA 6 below.

During the events of Chapter 1, which concludes with Jason and Lucia fighting their way out of a hospital against Mendez’s men, the Key Lento house burns to the ground. The owners of the hard drive that Jason and Lucia stole want the item back, and they burn the house down in order to get it.

Naturally, this is a major blow, both to Jason and Lucia and to you as the player. GTA 6 emphasizes saving money in the house’s floorboard stash, so you might have saved a tidy sum of cash before the house burns down. However, following Chapter 1, the entire area around Jason’s safehouse is marked in red, which indicates a major police presence.

This is basically the game’s way of telling you it’s not safe to return to the house. However, you can fully return to the Key Lento house when there are cops around it . You can also wait until the back half of GTA 6, when the police have left the area entirely, giving you free rein to explore the remains.

title: LCS : OpTic Gaming tient sa première recrue
content:
Le retour d’OpTic Gaming en LCS commence à prendre forme. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , la célèbre organisation nord-américaine devrait recruter Christian « KryRa » Rahaian pour la saison 2027. Âgé de 21 ans, le jungler canado-roumain deviendrait ainsi la première recrue du nouveau projet d’OpTic, qui remplacera Dignitas dans le championnat nord-américain. Le vétéran Juan « Contractz » Garcia aurait également été envisagé pour ce poste, mais la structure aurait finalement privilégié le jeune joueur de Disguised.

Après trois années passées dans les compétitions académiques nord-américaines, KryRa avait découvert les LCS en 2026 sous les couleurs de Disguised. Une première expérience compliquée, marquée par des problèmes de visa qui avaient retardé ses débuts, puis par des résultats décevants tout au long de la saison. Son équipe n’avait remporté que cinq séries sur l’ensemble de l’année, avant de sauver sa place dans l’élite lors du tournoi de promotion. Battus initialement par Maryville University (1-3), KryRa et ses coéquipiers avaient finalement pris leur revanche en finale (3-0), après un parcours réussi dans le lower bracket.

Cette arrivée potentielle marque surtout le début d’une nouvelle aventure pour OpTic Gaming. Absente des LCS depuis 2019, l’organisation américaine fera son retour en 2027 dans le cadre d’un partenariat avec Riot Games. Elle récupérera la place de Dignitas, qui conservera néanmoins la propriété de son slot. Lors de son premier passage dans la ligue, entre 2018 et 2019, OpTic n’avait jamais réussi à s’imposer parmi les meilleures équipes, avec une cinquième place comme meilleur résultat. La structure avait ensuite quitté la compétition après son rachat par Immortals.

Pour cette nouvelle tentative, OpTic entend repartir de zéro avec un effectif entièrement renouvelé. KryRa serait donc la première pièce d’un projet encore largement à construire, tandis que l’ancien manager général de Dignitas, Jonathon, devrait également rejoindre l’organisation. Reste désormais à connaître l’identité des quatre autres titulaires qui accompagneront le jungler en 2027. Avec le retour du célèbre Green Wall, les LCS s’apprêtent en tout cas à retrouver l’une des communautés les plus emblématiques de l’esport nord-américain.

title: Nvidia Adds Roughly $1 Trillion in Value as Jensen Huang Returns as CEO
content:
Nvidia added roughly $1 trillion in market value in the first hour and a half of trading on Monday, after its board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive 11 days after he resigned. The shares were up 33.76% at $167.91 at 11:11am ET, which is 4:11pm UTC, according to Google Finance . That lifted the chipmaker’s market value to about $4.04 trillion, from roughly $3 trillion at Friday’s close of $125.53.

The jump reverses a large part of the slide that followed Huang’s exit on 12 November. Friday’s close left the stock within a dollar or so of its 52-week low of $124.50, and almost half below its 52-week high of $243.37. The board’s decision, announced before the US market opened, is covered in full in our report on Huang’s reinstatement .

The shares opened at $167.04 and traded between $156.93 and $171.50 in the first part of the session. Volume had already passed 400 million shares by late morning, well above the stock’s average of about 225 million a day. With about 24.1 billion shares outstanding, each dollar on the share price is worth roughly $24 billion in market value.

On those numbers, the morning’s rise of more than $42 a share added about $1 trillion to Nvidia’s value. The figure will move through the day, but it is an unusually large one-day move even for a company of Nvidia’s size. It also suggests how much of Nvidia’s recent fall investors tied to the leadership crisis rather than to the business itself. The gain on Monday helped lift the wider US market at the open, according to our earlier report.

The board’s change of heart took just six days. Nvidia’s 12 November announcement , also filed with the SEC as a Form 8-K exhibit , said Huang had resigned as president, chief executive and director with immediate effect. It named chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while the board began a search for a permanent successor, looking at internal and external candidates. Huang left after reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for China, according to Reuters, and Beijing has denied the allegation.

As recently as 17 November, the board said it did not intend to bring him back, as our report on the board’s rejection covered. Monday’s filing with the SEC said the board voted unanimously for his return after “a series of discussions and meetings” with him. It said it had received input from “senior levels of the United States government” and was confident his return “poses no national security risk”.

title: GTA 6 Hacker Walks Free on the Day He Is Sentenced
content:
The hacker who stole unfinished GTA 6 footage from Rockstar Games in 2022 is out of custody. Arion Kurtaj, 21, from Oxford, was sentenced to seven years at Woolwich Crown Court and released on license the same day, after serving most of that time. The judge told him: "Don't let this happen again."

Kurtaj pleaded guilty last Monday at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar hack and a handful of other offenses. He carried them out at 16 and 17 as part of the teen hacking gang Lapsus$. He was sentenced and freed on the same day, having served the majority of a seven-year term.

He was first given an indefinite stay in a secure hospital because of the severity of his autism. In an unusual move, he was later judged fit to stand trial and moved to a normal prison in January.

The judge, Mr Justice Turner, told him "you are a very talented young man" before issuing the warning. Kurtaj stood and smiled when he was sentenced.

Kurtaj has been given a Serious Crime Prevention Order that lasts five years. It restricts his activity online and bars him from using Telegram and Discord.

City of London Police said the case highlights the dangers that young people can end up being drawn to online. His defence team said he found the online world a more comfortable way of interacting with other people. They said his connection to Lapsus$ gave him a sense of community.

title: LEC : la Karmine Corp s’offre SkewMond (off.)
content:
Après plusieurs jours de rumeurs, la Karmine Corp a officialisé ce lundi l’arrivée de Rudy « SkewMond » Semaan dans son équipe League of Legends. Considéré comme l’un des meilleurs junglers européens, le Français quitte G2 Esports après deux saisons couronnées de succès. Passé par la LFL sous les couleurs de BDS Academy, il avait rejoint les Samouraïs avec le statut de grand espoir avant de rapidement s’imposer au plus haut niveau. Avec quatre titres consécutifs en LEC entre 2025 et 2026, SkewMond s’est affirmé comme l’une des révélations majeures de la scène européenne.

Ce transfert représente un renfort de premier plan pour la Karmine Corp, qui sort d’une saison 2026 encourageante, marquée notamment par un quart de finale aux Worlds, mais sans le moindre trophée. Le Français prendra la place de Yike, pourtant auteur de prestations convaincantes et désormais annoncé du côté de Fnatic. SkewMond retrouvera notamment Caliste, autre grand talent français de sa génération, avec lequel il tentera de ramener la KC au sommet de l’Europe.

Le recrutement de SkewMond n’était pourtant pas prévu initialement. Mais la décision de G2 de profondément remanier son effectif a ouvert une opportunité inattendue. Encore sous contrat jusqu’en 2028, le jungler avait rapidement fait de la Karmine Corp sa destination privilégiée, malgré l’intérêt d’autres formations, dont Vitality. Cette dernière aurait même envisagé un échange impliquant Naak Nako, alors courtisé par G2 pour remplacer BrokenBlade. Une opération finalement abandonnée après le départ du toplaner turc vers LYON en LCS. La KC a donc pu conclure le transfert moyennant une indemnité dont le montant n’a pas été officiellement communiqué.

Sauf nouvelle surprise, SkewMond devrait être l’unique changement du cinq de départ de la Karmine Corp pour 2027. Le club français a déjà prolongé son midlaner kyeahoo jusqu’à la fin de l’année prochaine et devrait conserver Canna, Caliste et Busio. Après avoir atteint les quarts de finale des derniers championnats du monde, l’objectif sera désormais de transformer cette progression en titres, en commençant par reconquérir le LEC.

title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, 11 Days After His Resignation
content:
Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, 11 days after he resigned. The board voted unanimously for his return on 23 November, reversing its position from just days earlier that it did not intend to bring him back.

Nvidia shares jumped more than 25% in early trading after the announcement. Interim chief executive Colette Kress will return to her role as chief financial officer.

The board said it reached the decision after “a series of discussions and meetings” with Huang, after which it was satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead NVIDIA”. It also said it had received input from senior levels of the United States government and was confident that Huang’s return poses no national security risk.

Board chair Harvey Jones said Huang is “the right person to lead NVIDIA” and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of the company’s stockholders, employees, partners and customers. The announcement was published in Nvidia’s filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission .

Huang said he was “honored to return” to lead what he called one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. He described the current period as the beginning of a new industrial revolution.

The return marks a complete turn from the board’s stance at Nvidia’s earnings call last week. Jones said then that the board did not intend to reinstate Huang, even after Huang said publicly that he would be honoured to return, a decision covered when Nvidia’s board rejected Huang’s offer to come back .

title: Viral Claim Says GTA 6 Profiles Players for Insurers and Employers, but There Is No Proof
content:
A viral claim that Grand Theft Auto VI builds psychological profiles of players and sells them to insurers, lenders and employers has spread across social media, but no evidence has been published to support it. The claim comes from an anonymous account on X that says it belongs to a former senior engine engineer at Rockstar North.

Rockstar Games and its parent company Take-Two Interactive have not commented on the allegations. No documents, network data or technical proof have been shared, and several details in the claim do not match public records about Take-Two.

The account claims Lens then scores each player for impulse control, risk tolerance, aggression and spending habits, and links that score to the player’s console account and IP address. It says the profiles go to a Take-Two subsidiary named Vantage Analytics, which allegedly licenses the models to insurance companies, a credit risk firm, a hiring platform and an advertising broker.

content:
SOL: enchant's Episode 2 update later this week adds the Hellond region and a Lancer-only Class Change, along with the game's first new server, Infinity. Developers laid out the thinking behind the major update in an interview with Inven Global. It’s the biggest patch since late August and arrives on Wednesday.

The interview featured Director Gyeong-myeong Kang, Planning Team Lead Jae-ho Hwang, and Business Division Director Jang-hwan Kim. The biggest change for anyone who’s been playing the game for a few months is a boss system that no longer runs on a fixed clock.

Hellond is set in a magic city, though all that’s available at launch is its entrance, with the team opting for a phased rollout. Kang said broader playable areas and more content will follow soon. How different is it to the existing Caltheon region? The monsters are said to be tough, there are new progression targets, while extra quests are designed to educate players on the region's lore. Essentially, you’ll do more than just hunt monsters.

Kang said the team wanted a clean break from the old map. "We wanted players to feel from the moment they step into Hellond that they have arrived somewhere completely different from Caltheon."

Hwang added that the Episode 2 title, Infinity, reflects hopes that growth and challenge continue without end.

Earlier bosses in SOL: enchant spawned at set times, which meant raiding on the clock, something that Hellond changes. Kang explained that "Hellond allows guild members to directly summon bosses and challenge them together whenever they choose."

title: Comment GTA 6 a explosé le record de League of Legends sur Twitch
content:
Treize ans après la sortie de GTA 5, l’attente était immense. Et les chiffres ont rapidement confirmé le phénomène. Lancé en novembre 2026, Grand Theft Auto VI a rassemblé plus de 7,9 millions de spectateurs simultanés sur l’ensemble des plateformes de streaming, selon les données de Streams Charts . Sur Twitch, le jeu aurait atteint un pic d’environ 3,3 millions de spectateurs, dépassant ainsi le précédent record de la catégorie League of Legends. Une performance d’autant plus impressionnante que le MOBA de Riot Games domine régulièrement les audiences grâce à ses grandes compétitions internationales, notamment les Worlds.

Mais comment expliquer un tel succès ? D’abord par l’attente exceptionnelle entourant le nouveau titre de Rockstar Games, plus d’une décennie après le précédent opus. Ensuite, par la mobilisation massive des créateurs de contenu, qui se sont précipités sur le jeu pour faire découvrir Vice City à leurs communautés. Certains streamers ont même voyagé jusqu’en Nouvelle-Zélande pour profiter du lancement avant les joueurs nord-américains. Entre premières découvertes, réactions en direct et curiosité des spectateurs, GTA 6 est rapidement devenu un événement collectif dépassant largement les frontières du jeu vidéo.

L’impact de GTA 6 ne s’est pas limité à Twitch. Le jeu a également attiré des millions de spectateurs sur YouTube et Kick, confirmant une mobilisation exceptionnelle à l’échelle mondiale. Toujours d’après Streams Charts , le temps de visionnage global sur Twitch aurait même progressé de 61 % sur la période étudiée par rapport aux deux jours précédant le lancement. Une véritable démonstration de force pour Rockstar, dont le nouveau titre a momentanément éclipsé les habituels poids lourds du streaming, des jeux compétitifs aux grandes compétitions esportives.

Reste maintenant à savoir si cet engouement pourra durer. Après un parcours sans faute lors des premières rencontres, les Français ont successivement dominé la Radosin Corp (4-0), composé de Radosin, ejby et Mozzarella, puis Ikkaku (4-1), l’équipe d’ExoTiiK, Rezears et yujin. Ancien champion du monde, Seikoo sort d’une saison terminée sous les couleurs de Manchester City Esports, tandis que juicy avait notamment remporté le Major de Paris avec la Karmine Corp en 2026, avant d’atteindre les demi-finales des Worlds. À leurs côtés, mtzr confirme son statut de grand espoir de la scène française. Malgré son absence parmi les clubs partenaires directement qualifiés pour le tournoi londonien, l’organisation saoudienne avait réussi à attirer Seikoo et juicy pour construire un effectif 100 % français. Grand ménage en LEC : 16 joueurs ne seront pas de retour en 2027
content:
La saison 2027 du LEC s’annonce bien différente de la précédente. Entre les changements opérés par G2, la reconstruction de Fnatic et les nombreux mouvements chez Shifters ou Vitality, aucune organisation n’a échappé au mercato. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , 16 des 50 joueurs présents lors du dernier segment de 2026 ne devraient pas retrouver leur place dans le championnat européen. Certains ont choisi de prendre du recul, d’autres ont annoncé leur retraite, tandis que plusieurs joueurs se retrouvent simplement sans équipe malgré leur expérience au plus haut niveau.

Parmi les absences les plus marquantes figure Upset, qui quitterait le LEC après huit années de compétition. L’AD Carry allemand aurait suscité l’intérêt de Fnatic, Vitality et même Cloud9, sans parvenir à convaincre une structure de lui faire une offre prioritaire. Même constat pour Wunder, dont le retour chez SK Gaming n’aura finalement duré qu’une saison. Du côté de GIANTX, Oscarinin et Flakked n’ont pas réussi à retrouver une place malgré l’intérêt de plusieurs organisations espagnoles. Leur ancien coéquipier français ISMA aurait quant à lui refusé des propositions de SK Gaming et Shifters, préférant ne pas s’engager dans ces projets.

D’autres joueurs ont déjà trouvé une nouvelle destination, mais devront poursuivre leur carrière loin du LEC. C’est notamment le cas de Skeanz et Serin, attendus chez Galions en LFL, ou encore de FIESTA, qui devrait rejoindre LØS au Brésil. Naak Nako prendra pour sa part la direction de la LCS avec LYON, malgré l’intérêt de plusieurs équipes européennes, dont G2 Esports. Chez NAVI, Maynter et Poby n’ont pas été conservés et cherchent toujours un nouveau projet. La situation est également compliquée pour Daglas et Way, qui quittent Team Heretics sans avoir trouvé de nouveau point de chute dans l’élite.

Enfin, certaines absences sont liées à des décisions personnelles. Après plusieurs années en LEC, nuc a annoncé vouloir prendre une pause dans sa carrière, tandis que Stend a officiellement raccroché la souris. Leur ancien coéquipier Paduck ne devrait pas non plus poursuivre l’aventure européenne et explorerait désormais des opportunités en Chine. Au total, près d’un tiers des joueurs du Summer Split 2026 manqueront à l’appel en 2027, illustrant la brutalité d’un mercato où même les vétérans et les talents confirmés ne sont plus assurés de conserver leur place. Une nouvelle génération tentera désormais de s’imposer dans un championnat profondément renouvelé.

title: Brawl Stars : les Worlds 2027 auront lieu à Paris
content:
Paris sera au cœur de l’esport mobile en 2027. Les prochains championnats du monde de Brawl Stars se dérouleront dans la capitale française, une annonce importante pour une discipline qui continue de gagner en visibilité. L’édition 2026 se tient actuellement au Japon, dans une enceinte pouvant accueillir plus de 10 000 spectateurs. Un signe de l’ampleur prise par la compétition, particulièrement populaire en Asie, où l’esport mobile occupe déjà une place majeure.

Cette arrivée en France pourrait représenter une opportunité intéressante pour les organisations françaises, encore relativement discrètes sur la scène compétitive de Brawl Stars. Plusieurs grands noms de l’esport international sont déjà engagés sur le jeu, notamment Natus Vincere, Team Heretics, FUT Esports, ZETA DIVISION ou encore Crazy Raccoon. Avec un championnat du monde organisé à domicile, de nouvelles structures pourraient être tentées de rejoindre l’aventure pour profiter de l’engouement autour de l’événement.

En parallèle, Supercell a annoncé l’extension de son programme de clubs partenaires, destiné à renforcer les liens entre l’éditeur et les organisations esportives. Les structures concernées peuvent notamment bénéficier d’un partage des revenus générés par les cosmétiques en jeu, ainsi que de contenus exclusifs à leurs couleurs, comme des émoticônes, sprays et icônes. Le dispositif prévoit également une meilleure visibilité officielle et des échanges privilégiés avec Supercell sur le développement de la scène compétitive.

Autre avantage important : les clubs partenaires peuvent, sous certaines conditions, conserver leurs points et leurs places qualificatives même en cas de changement d’effectif. De quoi apporter davantage de stabilité aux projets sportifs et rendre l’investissement plus intéressant sur le long terme. À l’approche des Worlds 2027 à Paris, ces nouvelles perspectives pourraient convaincre plusieurs organisations françaises de tenter leur chance sur Brawl Stars, sans nécessairement engager les budgets considérables exigés par certaines autres disciplines. Reste à savoir si cette occasion permettra à la scène tricolore de franchir un nouveau cap.

title: LEC : Sjokz annonce une longue pause après plus de dix ans sur League of Legends
content:
C’est une annonce qui ne manquera pas de marquer les habitués du LEC. Ce samedi 21 novembre, Eefje « Sjokz » Depoortere a révélé qu’elle allait prendre une pause prolongée de ses activités d’animatrice au début de l’année 2027. Présente sur la scène compétitive de League of Legends depuis 2013, la Belge souhaite désormais prendre du temps pour elle, après plus d’une décennie passée à enchaîner les événements. Dans une vidéo publiée sur X, elle a expliqué envisager une absence de deux, trois, voire quatre mois, sans fixer de date précise pour son retour. Une décision réfléchie depuis longtemps, qui bénéficie du soutien de Riot Games.

L’animatrice a notamment évoqué plusieurs épreuves personnelles, dont la disparition de proches, ainsi que la nécessité de prendre davantage soin de sa santé physique et mentale. Sjokz a révélé avoir reçu un diagnostic de dépression clinique et s’être rapprochée de l’épuisement professionnel. Après des années à parcourir le monde pour couvrir les plus grandes compétitions, elle souhaite désormais s’accorder une véritable période de repos. Si elle n’exclut pas de continuer à streamer occasionnellement, aucune décision n’a encore été prise à ce sujet.

Cette annonce intervient dans un contexte particulièrement difficile pour Sjokz, récemment visée par une importante vague de harcèlement sur les réseaux sociaux. L’animatrice avait notamment été prise pour cible après ses commentaires concernant la décision de G2 Esports de se séparer de Perkz, à la suite des propos controversés de ce dernier sur l’avortement. La polémique avait pris une nouvelle ampleur après l’intervention du streamer américain Asmongold. Sjokz a toutefois tenu à préciser que ces événements n’avaient joué aucun rôle dans sa décision, celle-ci étant envisagée depuis bien avant les récentes controverses.

De son côté, Riot Games aurait pleinement soutenu cette démarche, allant même jusqu’à proposer à Sjokz d’apparaître lors du lancement du LEC 2027 afin d’éviter toute confusion sur son avenir au sein de la compétition. Une proposition qui témoigne de la confiance maintenue entre les deux parties. Présente à chaque édition des Worlds depuis 2013, comme intervieweuse ou animatrice, la Belge est devenue l’un des visages les plus reconnaissables de l’esport mondial. Son absence se fera forcément ressentir lors de la reprise du championnat européen en janvier, mais il ne s’agit pas d’un départ définitif. Pour Sjokz, la priorité est désormais de retrouver un meilleur équilibre avant d’envisager son retour sur scène.
